clusters.description: High usage and assist share with a balanced shot diet; guards and wings who run the offense (Brunson, Maxey, Durant).
clusters.name: Lead creator

clusters.description: Moderate usage, low assist share, most shots from three (Camara, Knueppel, Miles Bridges).
clusters.name: Spacing wing

clusters.description: Low usage, some playmaking, highest steal rate and above-average rim attempts (Derrick White, Dyson Daniels, Anunoby).
clusters.name: Two-way connector

clusters.description: Big-man rebounding and blocks with a real three-point share (Holmgren, Mobley, Myles Turner).
clusters.name: Stretch big

clusters.description: High usage and assist share, few threes, rim-heavy and strong defensive rebounding (Jokić, Sengun, Scottie Barnes).
clusters.name: Interior hub

clusters.description: Almost no threes, three in four shots at the rim, elite offensive rebounding and blocks (Gobert, Jarrett Allen, Zubac).
clusters.name: Rim runner

label: 2026-27 · projected
limitations: Projected: no 2026-27 minutes played yet. Each player is drawn from 2025-26 numbers.
Size is value over replacement: (BPR + 2.0) x share of a full season's minutes in 2025-26. It is descriptive, not a forecast, a team rating or a verdict.
BPR is a descriptive model estimate under lineup confounding, not causal.
Derived archetypes describe one season's statistical style, not a listed position.
Fit outline shows continuity only: whether the player appeared for this team in 2025-26. It does not measure how well players complement each other.
White space is the gap to the fullest roster in this view, not a target or a need.
Players without a value or 2025-26 minutes are unknown and never sized as zero; team totals are lower bounds.
Current team comes from the dated NBA player index, not prior-season participation.
Current association observed at acquisition, not backdated to season start.
Listed measurements are not combine measurements; career rates excluded.
